thesis.company_overview:
Affirm Holdings, Inc. (AFRM) operates a next-generation payment network that sells point-of-sale instalment financing to consumers and conversion economics to merchants. Consumers split purchases into fixed-instalment or interest-bearing plans, including through the Affirm Card; merchants pay a fee for incremental basket conversion and higher average order value. Revenue therefore mixes merchant network fees, card and processing income, and interest income on loans held, with originations routed through warehouse facilities and Affirm ABS securitization trusts. A segment revenue breakdown was not available for this issuer; see the latest annual report for business-line detail. Geographic revenue breakdown was also not available in the supplied XBRL snapshot, so no geographic split is asserted here.

Scale is now evident in reported figures: $4.26B of trailing-twelve-month revenue and $1.93B of trailing-twelve-month net income, against $15.79B of total assets, $10.31B of total liabilities and $5.48B of shareholders' equity at the fiscal year ended 2026-06-30.

The moat is underwriting IP plus two-sided network scale rather than a regulatory franchise. The transformer-based real-time risk model is designed to approve thin-file borrowers at checkout, widening the funnel without loosening aggregate credit standards; that edge monetises through merchant integrations — the reported Antom (Ant International) and Crate & Barrel additions widen acceptance. The funding stack of warehouse capacity and recurring ABS issuance is a scale advantage and simultaneously the binding constraint: the model is balance-sheet-intensive and its cost of capital sets the terminal economics. The moat is therefore real but partial and rate-sensitive, which is why the market price embeds a growth and discount-rate path the base-case DCF cannot reproduce.
thesis.competitor_analysis: No peer set was produced for AFRM in this run — the peer-screen data fetch returned no usable comps — so the competitive read here is structural rather than multiple-based, and it is a data-coverage gap, not a suppression of available evidence. Sector economics dominate: buy-now-pay-later is capital-intensive and funding-sensitive, so scale of ABS/warehouse capacity and underwriting IP, not distribution alone, decides who earns excess returns. Affirm competes on differentiated risk technology — the transformer-based real-time underwriting model extended to thin-file borrowers at checkout — versus merchant-funded, balance-sheet-light structures and versus incumbent card rails, and the reported Antom and Crate & Barrel integrations are share-gaining evidence on the merchant side. On valuation, the only relative anchor available is the issuer's own history: TTM EV/EBITDA of 26.8x versus a five-year median of 36.8x, a p25 of 27.9x and a p90 of 41.6x, classified as cheap against that band. Peer-relative premium or discount conclusions are not asserted, because no peer multiple was supplied.
key_takeaways: The call is HOLD on relative value, not on franchise quality: the $77.89 market price sits above the entire published fundamental band of $28.10–$46.84 produced by the surviving 10-year DCF (mid $37.47, WACC 12.61%, terminal growth 3.0%).

thesis.narrative:
Affirm Holdings (AFRM) at $77.89 trades above its entire published fundamental band of $28.10–$46.84. The one valuation method that survived this run — a 10-year DCF at a 12.61% WACC, revenue growth fading from 39.0% in FY1 to 3.0% in FY10 (21.0%/yr average) and a 3.0% perpetuity rate — returns $37.47, with an own-range of $29.98–$44.97. Reverse-engineering the quote: holding that growth fade fixed, $77.89 implies a ~9.31% discount rate; holding the 12.61% WACC fixed, it implies ~29.4%/yr revenue growth held flat for ten years. A flat 29.4% is a different construct from a 39.0%→3.0% fade averaging 21.0%, and that spread — not a claim that the market is irrational — is why the stance is HOLD rather than Buy.

The supportive side is genuine and quantified. Momentum is constructive at +6.4% over one year, 74% up the 52-week range and -13.9% off the high; TTM revenue of $4.26B and TTM net income of $1.93B show the platform has crossed into real profitability, with $5.48B of equity against $15.79B of assets. TTM EV/EBITDA of 26.8x versus a five-year median of 36.8x classifies the multiple as cheap on its own history, and the catalyst tape is positive — net sentiment +1.22, led by the reported Antom and Crate & Barrel merchant wins and the transformer-underwriting rollout.

The bear arithmetic is equally concrete. Over the last 90 days insiders were net sellers of [target withheld] with zero open-market purchases and a largest single sale of [target withheld], and the market price already sits at the 94th percentile of the Monte Carlo distribution (mean [target withheld]). If growth converges on the fade schedule rather than the flat 29.4% the price implies, the DCF lands at $37.47 — 0.48x the market — and the published band of $28.10–$46.84 acts as a floor, not a target. With the point withheld and one method only, HOLD is the honest read: the franchise is compounding, but the multiple has already banked the fade.

thesis.valuation_overview: Only one valuation method survived this run: a 10-year DCF built on FY1 revenue growth of 39.0% fading linearly to 3.0% by FY10 (21.0% average), a 12.61% WACC and a 3.0% perpetuity growth rate, returning $37.47 within an own-range of $29.98–$44.97. No comparable-company set was produced — the peer screen returned no usable data for this ticker — so there is no comps cross-check and no DDM, leaving the DCF to carry the full evidence weight at a 0.85 method weight. That lone method lands at 0.48x the $77.89 market price, outside the [0.5x, 2x] single-method calibration band, so the point target is withheld rather than published: $37.47 is the only available number and stamping it as a 12-month target would be false precision on a single far-from-market method. The published band of $28.10–$46.84 is best read as a fundamental floor. The reverse-DCF explains the divergence: holding the growth fade fixed, $77.89 implies a ~9.31% discount rate against the model's 12.61% WACC; holding WACC fixed, it implies ~29.4%/yr growth held flat for ten years against a 21.0% average fade.
